text:
alice-nguyen: heads-up — I just flipped the new rate-policy canary to 10% for the outbound inference API at 09:03 UTC. The change reduces per-tenant burst window from 120s->60s and lowers soft quota from 6req/s->4req/s. rolling via infra tool rctl, canary id c-2026-03-rate1

ben-mathews: noted. any smoke results yet?

alice-nguyen: initial health looks ok, logs show the canary hosts are healthy. seeing a small bump in 429s for a couple tenants in the canary group: 0.02% -> 0.4% request rate on 429 in the first 5 minutes.

luis-support: support queue has 3 tickets from canary customers complaining about increased 429s and one mentions "auth failure" but that looks like client-side retry exhaustion and then token refresh errors. sharing ticket ids 4921, 4923, 4927.

carla_ops: @alice-nguyen can you paste the exact headers customers are seeing? specifically x-rate-limit-remaining / reset. also which AZs are in the canary?

alice-nguyen: sample header from logs:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 240
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 161
x-rate-limit-window: 60
retry-after: 30
```
Canary hosts are in us-west1a and us-west1b (subset of region).

mike-enginfra: the policy reduced burst window and token bucket depth. some SDKs do aggressive in-process batching which suddenly exceeds the smaller burst. We should surface SDK guidance in the error body (eg backoff header).

luis-support: customers report SDKs retrying quickly then failing token refresh: sequence looks like A) token refresh fails with 401 B) client retries with expired token - this might look like auth issue but root is they retried while under 429 throttle.

alice-nguyen: agreed. I'm seeing correlated 401s in the logs immediately after repeated 429s from same client IPs. Our auth service rate-limits token refresh endpoints separately; they hit a different quota.

ben-mathews: we need a quick mitigation path. Options: 1) pause canary rollback 2) increase canary to 25% and revert the burst window change only for canary 3) add an exception rule for token refresh endpoints. Thoughts?

carla_ops: my vote is rollback the burst window change for the canary only (option 2 but revert the burst size) — that keeps the overall policy work intact but avoids breaking SDK retry patterns. rollback plan: rctl canary update --id c-2026-03-rate1 --set burst_window=120 --set soft_quota=6 then watch for 10m.

mike-enginfra: +1. Also add a temporary tweak to the auth rate limiter to be more permissive for canary tenant IDs (we can add header X-Canary: c-2026-03-rate1). That buys time without global change.

sre-oncall-bot: ALERT: 429 surge detected on canary group c-2026-03-rate1 (rate: 0.42% over baseline). Threshold breach at 1773001280.

eva-product: flagging: some product teams already built dashboards and will see this as regression. we should coordinate a short customer-facing note if we rollback.

alice-nguyen: executing rollback for burst_window now: running command: rctl canary update --id c-2026-03-rate1 --set burst_window=120 --set soft_quota=6 --comment "rollback after early 429 spike"

alice-nguyen: command returned success, config propagated to canary hosts. monitoring for 10m.

ben-mathews: starting a quick smoke: curling a high-rate test tenant in the canary group:
```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer" &
done
```
observing 1-2 429s in the first 30s then stabilized.

luis-support: support tickets updated: told affected customers we are rolling back adjustments on canary hosts, asked them to confirm if their SDK behavior normalizes.

carla_ops: after 8m, 429s back down to baseline 0.03%. auth 401 correlates also dropped. good signal.

mike-enginfra: follow-ups: 1) add canary-aware header so auth has separate budget; 2) revamp SDK retry guidance to honor Retry-After header and jitter; 3) longer canary with gradual stepdown of burst window instead of single jump. I'll open infra tickets.

alice-nguyen: creating rollout postmortem doc link: https://intranet/redwood/canary-postmortems/1773001123 — will add metrics, logs and timeline.

eva-product: please also add a short customer-facing note template (we can send to growth/customer success) that says we briefly lowered burst allowance, saw transient 429s for heavy batchers, rolled back, and will re-run a phased rollout with SDK guidance.

ben-mathews: agreed. marking this thread resolved for now. if we see another spike we'll trigger full rollback across regions. :white_check_mark:
